title: Mystery Is My Hobby
paragraphs: A syndicated mystery series centered on crime writer and amateur detective Barton Drake, who becomes involved in murder investigations and helps unravel cases through observation and deduction.

Crime/mystery drama centered on mystery writer and amateur sleuth Barton Drake with police companion Inspector Noah Danton. Surviving material circulated through syndication packages that reused stories and program numbers, making universal episode numbering and many air dates unsafe.
The run breaks into several distinct periods: Murder Is My Hobby network identity (1945 to 1946) and Mystery Is My Hobby syndicated packages (1947 to 1949).

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Glenn Langan (performer), Norman Field (performer), Betty Lou Gerson (performer), Bruce Buehl (announcer), Dave Titus (director), Fred Howard (writer), and Jack Edwards Jr. (performer).
Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]].

The stories often return to murder and homicide, deception, false identity and framing, wealth, valuables and inheritance, marriage, spouses and family conflict, artists, writing and media, and politics, elections and public office.
The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Postwar radio detective and mystery boom, Repackaged syndicated radio drama, and Mystery-writer detective protagonist.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]], [[show|the-whistler|The Whistler]], [[show|screen-directors-playhouse|Screen Directors Playhouse]], [[show|the-great-gildersleeve|The Great Gildersleeve]], and [[show|the-railroad-hour|The Railroad Hour]].
